committed_before: any structure or crossover it names was built or read on seeds 61, 62 and 63, on build 846, and before the score it judges (gsd-law-score-8) read any of them. It is written after criterion 4's reading (seeds 51 to 53, 2026-11-23), which missed S1 on five pairs and S2 on one, and it is written fresh because of it: criterion 4 stays as it was judged, its reading committed beside it. Its strips, tubes, trees and soups differ from criterion 4's (widths 24, 40 and 56, tubes 6 by 6 and 12 by 12, trees of paths of 4 and 16 beside the paths of 8, a soup whose largest cycle is 12,288 nodes) or are read on new seeds; criterion 3's seventeen structures are read again on seeds 61 to 63.
question: Does a settled reading describe the graph's own scale, on a graph that stopped changing and is one piece? Study 174's bundle of 2026-11-23 09:52Z showed both failing: none of its five finds from empty or random grows with N as the ring its probes read (reach x 0.68 to x 2.02 from 16,384 to 65,536, where a ring grows x 4), one of them a soup of cycles whose largest piece was 14% of the graph, and 53 of the 61 finds report 23 classes scoring only on rungs the decisions call never equilibrated (the operator, 2026-11-23 11:21: "if you say the current scoring is off, and reduces the existing list from 62 to 4-14 then that is of course the thing we need to do first"). Criterion 4 answered it in part: every exact structure still settles, and a piece under half the graph earns nothing; but a tree of long paths settled one pair at d 1.30 whose reach then grew as d 3.0 at the next size, so a pair can look like a dimension in the middle of a crossover, and a strip or a tube that is a line at the size read settles as the line it is, which criterion 4's S1 forbade.
a_reading: criterion 3's rule (more than half of a rung's seeds read; the mean of those that read), and a seed counts only where its chain stopped changing: its rung's terminal class is EQUILIBRATED_ACTIVE, EQUILIBRATED_LOW_ACTIVITY, AT_REST or FROZEN_OR_ABSORBING, or that chain's own last chunk reads frozen. A seed that does not count still counts against the reading: more than half of all the rung's seeds must read and count. A built structure is a graph that does not change, so every seed of it counts.
connected: a chain is read at a size only where its largest piece holds at least 4,096 nodes (as before) and at least half of the graph: the decisions' connectivity floor (policy connectivity_floor 0.5 from 1,024).
the_sizes: from the smallest size at or above 4,096, the next size is the smallest at least three times the last: the fleet's ladder steps by four, and a table family or a judged structure built at other sizes is read at the sizes nearest that step. A pair is two such sizes one after the other.
settles: a probe settles at a pair when it reads at both sizes and |x_b - x_a| <= r(p, b) * (x_a + x_b) / 2, r the probe's relative margin at the pair's larger size
scale: a pair (a, b) holds its scale when the reach r (the half-volume radius, the mean over the seeds that count) grows as the d the score reads at b: |ln(r_b / r_a) - ln(b / a) / d_b| <= q ln(b / a) / d_b + 1 / (2 r_a) + 1 / (2 r_b) + z sqrt((se_a / r_a)^2 + (se_b / r_b)^2), d_b the median of the probes read at b, se the standard error of the counted seeds' reach (0 where one seed counts), z = 2. A probe settles at a pair, and the Einstein relation holds there, only where the pair holds its scale; a probe that reads at both sizes of a pair that does not hold its scale keeps its one point for reading. A pair without a reach at either size does not hold its scale. New in this criterion: a pair (a, b) whose chain also reads at the next size c of the score's steps keeps its scale only if (b, c) does not break it, a step breaking when both its reaches and d are read and it does not hold its scale: a dimension that the next size's reach does not grow by was a crossover on its way, and the probes settled on it settled nothing. A pair whose next size is not read, or is read without a reach, keeps its own verdict.
einstein: all four probes agree at a pair when all four settle there and, at the larger size, both |d_s - 2 d_V / d_w| and |d_s - 2 d_B / d_w| are at most tau * d_s: d_V and d_B are each the mass dimension d_f of the relation, at a pair that holds its scale
points: at a pair, the probes that settle (0 to 4) and one more where all four agree: 0 to 5; the fifth is the landscape's 5th band

training.families: every family of table_holds' with_a_dimension, the lattices of one to four dimensions, both quotients, the Sierpinski gasket and carpet and the uniform random tree, each probe at the sizes table_holds holds it at (from its from_nodes)
training.triples: seeds 0, 1, 2; 3, 4, 5; 6, 7, 8 of a size the table holds ten seeds at, and 0, 1, 2 alone where it holds three: a fleet rung's three seeds
training.reach_rule: q is the smallest value of its grid at least twice the widest training excess, max(0, |ln(r_b / r_a) - ln(b / a) / d_b| - (1 / (2 r_a) + 1 / (2 r_b) + z sqrt((se_a / r_a)^2 + (se_b / r_b)^2))) / (ln(b / a) / d_b), over every pair from 4,096 of every training family's triples, d_b the median of the probes the triple reads at b. A pair whose excess would set q above the grid's largest value sets q to it and is listed.
training.form_chosen_in_view_of_training: the allowance's form (half a step of the reach at each size, two standard errors of the seeds' reach) was chosen with the training set in view: an exact lattice's reach is a whole number of steps and moves in whole steps (the A4 lattice reads 8 and 10 at 20,736 and 65,536), and the uniform random tree's reach spreads by about a fifth between seeds. No held-out structure was read when it was chosen.
training.written_to: the reach block of graph_scale_dynamics/resources/calibration/score_margins.json, by tools/score_known_answers.py --write, never by hand
training.next_step: the rule has no parameter of its own: it reads the same q, z and half step at the next step as at the pair, trained as criterion 4 trained them; a training family whose next step breaks would be listed

held: a probe is held where the table holds that family at that size (table_holds' bands) for a family of the table, where 764's criterion gave it a band for any other structure, and from 16,384 for the random geometric graph in three dimensions; a probe held at a size that does not read there is reported, not a miss: the score judges settling, the probes' own judged sets judge reading

crossover_rule: a strip or a tube is judged at every pair whose smaller size is at least twice as long as the strip or tube is wide (judged_from_n names that size); a pair from a square or a cube is reported, not judged.

predictions.K1: criterion 3's K1 under the score with its scale, its next step and its floor: every probe held at both sizes of a pair and reading at both settles at that pair
predictions.K2: criterion 3's K2 likewise: every structure held on all four probes at both sizes of a pair and reading all four at both is in the fifth band there
predictions.K3: criterion 3's K3 likewise: no probe that must refuse settles at any pair
predictions.K4: criterion 3's K4 likewise: the law score of a chain from empty given a structure's readings is 0 for every structure of K3, and its points at its top pair are 5 for every structure of K2
predictions.S1: at every judged pair of a strip or a tube, a probe settles or the Einstein relation holds only where the d read at the larger size is below 1.5: a strip or a tube is read only as the line it is at that size, never as the plane or the volume its width shows its probes
predictions.S2: no subdivided random tree (paths of 4, 8 and 16) is read as a ring: at no pair where a probe settles or the Einstein relation holds is the d read at its larger size below 1.5
predictions.S3: neither soup of cycles earns a point at a pair whose larger size has its largest piece under half the graph
predictions.reach_rule: q, trained by the reach rule on the installed table, is the one in force

passes: when K1 to K4 and S1 to S3 hold on every case; every miss is listed. A sandbox set, to 65,664 nodes.
measured_by: graph_scale_dynamics/research/probes_known_answers.measure, the probes of this tree (analysis-5.3.0, estimator e639334808716378), each structure built by 764's builder; each crossover built by research/probes_known_answers.build
reported_beside: every judged pair's reach, the d its growth implies and the d read, and whether its next step broke it; what the score gave each pair without the next step (gsd-law-score-7) and without scale or floor (gsd-law-score-6); the pairs from a square or a cube.
what_follows: If K1 to K4 and S1 to S3 hold, the score reads only counted seeds, a connected piece and pairs that hold their scale and whose next step does not break it (gsd-law-score-8), and study 174's finds are read again with it, first from its bundle and then from the bundle its folder writes on 846. It decides nothing: no gate, rung or let-through reads the score. If one misses, the miss is named with its structure and pair, and the score in force stays gsd-law-score-6 in 846.
